lessons.title: Dimensions of seed quality
lessons.html:
What 'quality' means for seed

Seed quality is multi-dimensional. A lot can be physically clean yet low in germination, or germinate well in the laboratory yet establish poorly in a cold, wet Free State spring. Assessment therefore combines several attributes, each measured by standardised methods so that results are reproducible and legally defensible.

Physical quality

  • Analytical purity: the proportion by mass of pure seed, other seeds and inert matter.
  • Other seed determination: counting seeds of other species, especially prohibited or restricted weeds, in a larger sample.
  • Moisture content: critical for storage life; high moisture accelerates deterioration and fungal growth.
  • Thousand-seed weight and size grading: used for planting-rate calculations and plate selection on planters.

Physiological quality

  • Germination: the percentage of seeds producing normal seedlings under optimal laboratory conditions.
  • Viability: whether seeds are alive, including dormant seeds, often assessed by the tetrazolium (TZ) test.
  • Vigour: the sum of properties that determine performance across a wide range of field conditions; vigour declines before germination does.
  • Dormancy: live seed that does not germinate under normally suitable conditions; common in freshly harvested wheat, sunflower and many pasture grasses.

Genetic quality

Varietal identity and purity: is the seed the cultivar claimed, and how many off-types are present? Assessed by grow-out tests, morphological examination, and laboratory methods such as protein electrophoresis or DNA markers.

Health quality

Seed-borne pathogens (fungi, bacteria, viruses) and insect infestation. Some are quarantine organisms relevant to phytosanitary certification.

Seed deterioration

Deterioration is inevitable and irreversible; its rate depends mainly on seed moisture and storage temperature. Membranes lose integrity, reserves are depleted and enzymes fail. Mechanical damage at harvest and processing, such as cracked seed coats in soybeans or beans, sharply increases deterioration and seedling abnormality.

lessons.title: Interpreting and applying test results
lessons.html:
From laboratory to decision

Results are only useful if they are correctly interpreted against standards, tolerances and the intended use.

Germination assessment

ISTA rules define how seedlings are evaluated:

  • Normal seedlings: show potential to develop into satisfactory plants, with essential structures (root system, shoot axis, cotyledons, terminal bud) intact or with only slight defects.
  • Abnormal seedlings: damaged, deformed or decayed essential structures.
  • Hard seeds: remain hard because they have not imbibed water, common in legumes.
  • Fresh ungerminated seeds: imbibed but dormant.
  • Dead seeds: soft, mouldy and not producing seedlings.

Only normal seedlings count towards the germination percentage. Conditions (substrate, temperature, light, duration, dormancy-breaking treatments) are specified per species in the rules.

Tolerances

Because results come from samples, two tests on the same lot will rarely agree exactly. ISTA tolerance tables define the maximum acceptable difference between replicates, between tests and between a test result and a declared or minimum standard. A result marginally below a standard may still be within tolerance; a lab must apply tolerances correctly before rejecting or accepting.

Vigour testing

Examples include accelerated ageing, electrical conductivity (especially for peas and soybeans), the cold test for maize and seedling growth rate tests. Vigour results help seed companies rank lots, decide which lots to sell first or carry over, and advise on planting in stressful conditions.

Quality decisions in practice

FindingPossible decision
Germination below standard, high abnormalsInvestigate mechanical damage; reject for certification or recondition
Low germination, high fresh ungerminatedDormancy suspected; retest with dormancy-breaking treatment or TZ
High moistureDry before storage
Prohibited weed seed foundLot may be unsaleable; re-clean if possible

Reporting

Report results on the correct certificate or report format with method references, sample and lot identification and any deviations. Never report results for tests not done to the stated method.

Key points

  • Seed quality has physical, physiological, genetic and health dimensions.
  • Only normal seedlings count in germination.
  • Vigour declines before germination and predicts field performance.
  • Apply ISTA tolerances before judging a result against a standard.
  • Moisture and temperature drive deterioration in storage.
